extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO staff (U.S. procedural audience)
extracted.subtask_short: US patent filing and access rules
extracted.subtask_description: Rules governing public access/confidentiality of USPTO application files and detailed fee schedules and surcharges for filing, search, examination, and related procedural transactions for U.S. patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-certified copies availability (§ 1.13(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-certified copies of patents, patent application publications and of any records, books, papers, or drawings within the jurisdiction of the USPTO and open to the public, will be furnished by the USPTO to any person upon payment of the appropriate fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.19(b) for fees; copies of other records or papers will be furnished to persons entitled thereto upon payment of the appropriate fee. See § 2.201 regarding trademark records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copies authentication (§ 1.13(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Certified copies of patents, patent application publications, trademark registrations and of any records, books, papers, or drawings within the jurisdiction of the USPTO and open to the public or persons entitled thereto will be authenticated by the seal of the USPTO and certified by the Director, or in his or her name, upon payment of the fee for the certified copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees for certified copies are set forth in the fee schedule (§ 1.19(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of patent application information (§ 1.14(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications that have not been published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) are generally preserved in confidence pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(a). Information concerning the filing, pendency, or subject matter of an application, including status information, and access to the application, will only be given to the public as set forth in § 1.11 or in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the baseline: unpublished applications are generally confidential; access only as allowed by statute or rules in § 1.11/§ 1.14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability — Patented applications and statutory invention registrations (§ 1.14(a)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The file of an application that has issued as a patent or published as a statutory invention registration is available to the public as set forth in § 1.11(a). A copy of the application-as-filed, the file contents, or a specific document may be provided upon request and payment of the appropriate fee (§ 1.19(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public access is routine for issued/published applications; fees apply for copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability — Published abandoned applications (§ 1.14(a)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The file of an abandoned published application is available to the public as set forth in § 1.11(a). Copies of the application-as-filed, the file contents, or a specific document in the file of the published application may be provided upon request and payment of the appropriate fee (§ 1.19(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication (even if abandoned) triggers public availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability — Published pending applications (§ 1.14(a)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the application-as-filed, the file contents, or a specific document in the file of a pending published application may be provided to any person upon request and payment of the appropriate fee (§ 1.19(b)). If a redacted copy was used for publication, the copy provided may be limited to the redacted copy. The Office will not provide access to the paper file of a pending application that has been published, except as provided in paragraph (c) or (i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published pending apps: electronic/file copies may be provided, but paper-file access is restricted except under specific provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability — Unpublished abandoned applications identified or relied upon (§ 1.14(a)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The file contents of an unpublished, abandoned application may be made available to the public if the application is identified in a U.S. patent, statutory invention registration, U.S. patent application publication, an international publication of a PCT application under Article 21(2), or a publication of an international registration under Hague Agreement Article 10(3). A copy may also be made available if benefit of the abandoned application is claimed under specified statutes in an application that has issued or published. Copies provided upon written request and payment of the appropriate fee (§ 1.19(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification requires providing specific application-identifying information (application number/serial number and filing date; first named inventor; title; filing date or other application-specific info) in the text of the identifying document; mere inclusion in a file paper is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability — Unpublished pending applications whose benefit is claimed (§ 1.14(a)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the file contents of an unpublished pending application may be provided to any person, upon written request and payment of the appropriate fee (§ 1.19(b)), if the benefit of the application is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) in an application that has issued as a U.S. patent or in an application that has published as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will not provide paper-file access of a pending application except as provided in paragraph (c) or (i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability — Unpublished pending applications incorporated by reference or otherwise identified (§ 1.14(a)(1)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the application as originally filed of an unpublished pending application may be provided to any person upon written request and payment of the appropriate fee (§ 1.19(b)) if the application is incorporated by reference or otherwise identified in a U.S. patent, statutory invention registration, U.S. patent application publication, an international publication under PCT Article 21(2), or a publication under Hague Agreement Article 10(3). The Office will not provide access to the paper file of a pending application except as provided in paragraph (c) or (i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation by reference or identification in an enumerated published document permits release of the application-as-filed copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: When petition for access or power to inspect is required (§ 1.14(a)(1)(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that were not published or patented, and that are not the subject of benefit claims or identification as described, are not available to the public. If an application is identified only in the file contents of another application (but not in the published patent/application), a granted petition for access or a power to inspect is necessary to obtain the application or a copy of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If identification is only buried in another application's file contents, formal petition or power to inspect is needed to obtain the materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicly communicable status information (§ 1.14(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The information that may be communicated to the public (i.e., status information) includes: (i) whether the application is pending, abandoned, or patented; (ii) whether the application has been published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b); (iii) the application 'numerical identifier' (eight-digit application number or six-digit serial number plus a filing/intl filing/national stage date); and (iv) whether another application claims the benefit of the application and, if so, the numerical identifier(s), the specified relationship (e.g., continuation), pendency/abandonment/patent status, and publication status under 35 U.S.C. 122(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the limited status metadata that can be released for applications preserved in confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic access to an application (§ 1.14(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a copy of the application file or access to the application may be made available pursuant to this section, the Office may at its discretion provide access to only an electronic copy of the specification, drawings, and file contents of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may restrict provision to electronic copies only; physical paper-file access is more limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to inspect — required written authority and signatories (§ 1.14(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to an application may be provided to any person if the application file is available and the application contains written authority (e.g., a power to inspect) granting access to such person. The written authority must be signed by: (1) the applicant; (2) a patent practitioner of record; (3) the assignee or an assignee of an undivided part interest; (4) the inventor or joint inventor; or (5) a registered attorney or agent named in the papers accompanying the application if a power of attorney has not been appointed under § 1.32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written authority is requisite for third-party access via the power-to-inspect mechanism; signature requirements are strictly enumerated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications reported to Department of Energy (§ 1.14(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that appear to disclose inventions relating to atomic energy are reported to the Department of Energy, which will be given access to the applications. Such reporting does not constitute a determination that the subject matter is useful, an invention, or in specified statutory categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting is procedural; it does not imply substantive determinations about the application content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may publish decisions of precedential value (§ 1.14(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any decision by the Director that would not otherwise be open to public inspection may be published or made available for public inspection if: (1) the Director believes the decision involves an interpretation of patent laws or regulations that would be of precedential value; and (2) the applicant is given notice and an opportunity to object in writing within two months on the ground that the decision discloses a trade secret or other confidential information. Objecting parties must identify deletions or explain why the entire decision must be withheld; time to request reconsideration and seek court review will be provided before portions are made public over objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant protections: notice, 2-month objection window, minimum 20 days to request reconsideration and seek court review before publication over objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to inventor of filing may be published (§ 1.14(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may publish notice in the Official Gazette as to the filing of an application on behalf of an inventor by a person who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest in the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mechanism for public notice of filings made on inventor's behalf by third parties with proprietary interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of international application files furnished under PCT (Home/Search/Examination Copy conditions) (§ 1.14(f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of international application files for international applications designating the U.S. and published under PCT Article 21(2), or copies of a document in such files, will be furnished in accordance with PCT Articles 30 and 38 and PCT Rules 94.2 and 94.3, upon written request including a showing that the publication occurred and that the U.S. was designated, and upon payment of the appropriate fee (§ 1.19(b)), if: (i) Home Copy — the international application was filed with the U.S. Receiving Office; (ii) Search Copy — the U.S. acted as the International Searching Authority (except the written opinion will not be available until 30 months from priority date); (iii) Examination Copy — the U.S. acted as the International Preliminary Examining Authority, an IPER has issued, and the United States was elected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different copies (Home/Search/Examination) have distinct conditions for release; fees and proof of publication/U.S. designation required; written opinion availability delayed for 30 months in Search Copy context.

rubrics_metrics.name: English translation of international publication (§ 1.14(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of an English language translation of a publication of an international application filed in the USPTO pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 154(d)(4) will be furnished upon written request showing the international publication and U.S. designation, and upon payment of the appropriate fee (§ 1.19(b)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation copies are available on proof of publication/U.S. designation and payment of specified fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic data and Examination Copy limitations under PCT (§ 1.14(f)(4)-(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographic data related to copies of an international application-as-filed will not be provided prior to international publication under PCT Article 21(2). Access to international application files under certain paragraphs will not be permitted with respect to the Examination Copy in accordance with PCT Article 38.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT rules restrict disclosure of bibliographic data and Examination Copy content prior to international publication or per PCT Article 38.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access by participating foreign intellectual property offices (§ 1.14(h)(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to an application-as-filed may be provided to any foreign IP office participating in a bilateral or multilateral priority document exchange agreement if the application contains written authority granting such access. Written authority authorizes the Office to provide (i) a copy of the application-as-filed and its related bibliographic data; (ii) a copy of the application-as-filed of any application whose filing date is claimed by the application and its bibliographic data; and (iii) the date of filing of the written authorization under this paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access is limited to participating foreign IP offices and requires written authority; the scope of provided materials is defined in subparagraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to file contents for foreign IP office requirements (§ 1.14(h)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to the file contents of an application may be provided to a foreign IP office that has imposed a requirement for information on a counterpart application where the foreign office is a party to a bilateral or multilateral agreement to provide the required information, and the application contains written authority granting such access. Written authority will be treated as authorizing the Office to provide the bibliographic data and any content of the application file necessary to satisfy the foreign office requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign IP office access can include substantive file content as necessary to meet counterpart office information requirements under agreement; written authorization is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written authority requirements for foreign office access (§ 1.14(h)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Written authority provided under paragraphs (h)(1) and (h)(2) must include the title of the invention (§ 1.72(a)), comply with the requirements of paragraph (c), and be submitted on an application data sheet (§ 1.76) or on a separate document (§ 1.4(c)). The written authority should be submitted before filing any subsequent foreign application in which priority is claimed to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal content and timing requirements for written authority to facilitate foreign-office exchanges; inclusion on ADS or separate document recommended prior to subsequent foreign filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access or copies in other special circumstances (§ 1.14(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office, either sua sponte or on petition, may provide access or copies of all or part of an application if necessary to carry out an Act of Congress or if warranted by other special circumstances. Any petition by a member of the public seeking access to copies of a pending or abandoned application preserved in confidence must include: (1) the fee set forth in § 1.17(g); and (2) a showing that access is necessary to carry out an Act of Congress or that special circumstances exist which warrant granting access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions for access require payment of specified fee and a substantive showing of necessity or special circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: International design applications — availability rules (§ 1.14(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to an international design application maintained by the Office as a designated office for national processing, the records may be made available as provided under paragraphs (a) through (i). For an international design application maintained by the Office as an office of indirect filing, records may be made available under paragraph (j)(1) where contained in the national processing file. If benefit of the international design application is claimed in a U.S. patent or published application, the file contents or copies may be made available upon written request and payment of the appropriate fee (§ 1.19(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International design application disclosure follows the same framework, with distinctions for capacity (designated office vs indirect filing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic filing fee for original (utility) patent applications (§ 1.16(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic fee for filing each application under 35 U.S.C. 111 for an original patent, except design, plant, or provisional applications: By a micro entity (§ 1.29) $70.00; By a small entity (§ 1.27(a)) $140.00; By a small entity if submitted via USPTO electronic filing system $70.00; By other than a small or micro entity $350.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entity-status discounts apply (micro, small); additional discount for small entity when submitted electronically as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic filing fee for original design patent applications (§ 1.16(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic fee for filing each application under 35 U.S.C. 111 for an original design patent: By a micro entity $60.00; By a small entity $120.00; By other than a small or micro entity $300.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patent filing fees are lower than utility; entity-status distinctions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic filing fee for original plant patent applications (§ 1.16(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic fee for filing each application for an original plant patent: By a micro entity $48.00; By a small entity $96.00; By other than a small or micro entity $325.00 (note: table shows other-than amounts inconsistent in chunk; refer to full table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant patent filing fees and entity-status distinctions apply; consult full table for current amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic fee for filing a provisional application (§ 1.16(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic fee for filing each provisional application: By a micro entity $65.00; By a small entity $130.00; By other than a small or micro entity $325.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional application basic filing fees have entity discounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic fee for filing a reissue of a patent (§ 1.16(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic fee for filing each application for the reissue of a patent: By a micro entity $120.00; By a small entity $240.00; By other than a small or micro entity $600.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue application fees are higher than provisional/design and vary by entity status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surcharge for late filing of fees or inventor's oath or missing claim (§ 1.16(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Surcharge for filing the basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, or the inventor’s oath or declaration on a date later than the filing date of the application, an application that does not contain at least one claim on the filing date, or an application filed by reference to a previously filed application (except provisional applications): By a micro entity $34.00; By a small entity $68.00; By other than a small or micro entity $170.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surcharges apply when certain required items are filed late or when the application lacks at least one claim at filing (subject to provisional exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Surcharge for late basic filing fee or cover sheet in provisional applications (§ 1.16(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Surcharge for filing the basic filing fee or cover sheet (§ 1.51(c)(1)) on a date later than the filing date of the provisional application: By a micro entity $13.00; By a small entity $26.00; By other than a small or micro entity $65.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller surcharges for late provisional cover sheet/fee compared to non-provisional late surcharges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional fee for independent claims in excess of three (§ 1.16(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the basic filing fee in an application, other than a provisional application, for filing or later presentation at any other time of each claim in independent form in excess of 3: By other than a small or micro entity $240.00 (table heading indicates entity-based amounts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent claim count above three incurs additional per-claim fees; multiple-dependent claims are treated separately per § 1.75(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: In addition to basic fee — fee for claims in excess of twenty (§ 1.16(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the basic filing fee in an application, other than a provisional application, for filing or later presentation at any other time of each claim (whether dependent or independent) in excess of 20: By a micro entity $40.00; By a small entity $80.00; By other than a small or micro entity $200.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All claims beyond 20 (dependent or independent) incur per-claim fees; multiple dependent claim counting addressed by § 1.75(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee for multiple dependent claim per application (§ 1.16(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the basic filing fee in an application, other than a provisional application, that contains, or is amended to contain, a multiple dependent claim, per application: By a micro entity $185.00; By a small entity $370.00; (other-than amounts shown in table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple dependent claims trigger a per-application fee in addition to normal claim fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination fee for utility applications (§ 1.16(o))
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination fee for each application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111 for an original patent, except design, plant, or provisional applications: By a micro entity $176.00; By a small entity $352.00; By other than a small or micro entity $880.00 (table also shows $925.00 in another column—consult full rule for current amount).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination fees vary by entity status; consult the official fee table for the precise current amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search fee for utility applications (§ 1.16(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: Search fee for each application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111 for an original patent, except design, plant, or provisional applications: By a micro entity $154.00; By a small entity $308.00; By other than a small or micro entity $770.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search fee is separate from examination fee and varies by entity status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search fee for design patents (§ 1.16(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: Search fee for each application under 35 U.S.C. 111 for an original design patent: By a micro entity $60.00; By a small entity $120.00; By other than a small or micro entity $300.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patent search fees are distinct and lower than utility search fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search fee for plant patents (§ 1.16(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: Search fee for each application for an original plant patent: By a micro entity $97.00; By a small entity $194.00; By other than a small or micro entity $485.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant patent search fees listed by entity status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search fee for reissue applications (§ 1.16(n))
rubrics_metrics.description: Search fee for each application for the reissue of a patent: (table entries for micro, small, other-than amounts provided; e.g., By a micro entity $154.00; By a small entity $308.00; By other than a small or micro entity $770.00 in the chunked tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue search fee exists and varies by entity; consult full table for definitive current amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination fee for design patents (§ 1.16(p))
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination fee for each application under 35 U.S.C. 111 for an original design patent: By a micro entity $140.00; By a small entity $280.00; By other than a small or micro entity $700.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design examination fees are lower than utility and are tiered by entity status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination fee for plant patents (§ 1.16(q))
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination fee for each application for an original plant patent: By a micro entity $145.00; By a small entity $290.00; By other than a small or micro entity $725.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant examination fees listed by entity status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination fee for reissue applications (§ 1.16(r))
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination fee for each application for the reissue of a patent: By a micro entity $510.00; By a small entity $1,020.00; By other than a small or micro entity $2,550.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue examination fees are substantially higher and tiered by entity status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application size fee for specification and drawings over 100 sheets (§ 1.16(s))
rubrics_metrics.description: Application size fee for any application filed under 35 U.S.C.111 for the specification and drawings which exceed 100 sheets of paper, for each additional 50 sheets or fraction thereof: By a micro entity $90.00; By a small entity $180.00; By other than a small or micro entity $450.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Size-based per-additional-50-sheet fees apply; count sheets carefully to avoid unexpected fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-electronic filing fee (§ 1.16(t))
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-electronic filing fee for any application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) filed on or after November 15, 2011, other than by the USPTO patent electronic filing system, except for a reissue, design, or plant application: By a small entity $200.00; By other than a small entity $400.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty fee for filing non-electronically (encourages electronic filing); micro-entity amount not shown in chunk — consult full table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional fee for DOCX nonconformity (§ 1.16(u))
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional fee for any application filed on or after January 17, 2024 under 35 U.S.C. 111 for an original patent, except design, plant, or provisional applications, where the specification, claims, and/or abstract does not conform to the USPTO requirements for submission in DOCX format: By a micro entity $86.00; By a small entity $172.00; By other than a small or micro entity $430.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee applies when submission format requirements (DOCX) are not met; added to encourage conformity to electronic format standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension fees for late replies pursuant to § 1.136(a) (§ 1.17(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension fees for reply within first through fifth months: For reply within first month — By a micro entity $47.00; small entity $94.00; other-than $235.00. For second month — By a micro entity $138.00; small entity $276.00; other-than $690.00. For third month — By a micro entity $318.00; small entity $636.00; other-than $1,590.00. For fourth month — By a micro entity $499.00; small entity $998.00; other-than $2,495.00. For fifth month — By a micro entity $679.00; small entity $1,358.00; other-than $3,395.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progressively larger extension fees apply the later the reply is filed; provisional applications are excepted where noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for proceedings before the PTAB (§ 1.17(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: For fees in proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, see § 41.20 and § 42.15 of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB proceeding fees are governed by separate sections; consult § 41.20/§ 42.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee for filing a request for prioritized examination (§ 1.17(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: For filing a request for prioritized examination under § 1.102(e): By a micro entity $903.00; By a small entity $1,806.00; By other than a small or micro entity $1,500.00 (note: chunked tables show multiple amounts; consult full rule for correct current figures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritized examination (track one) requires payment of an additional fee, with entity-status distinctions; verify current amounts in official fee schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for first request for continued examination (RCE) (§ 1.17(e)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: For filing a first request for continued examination pursuant to § 1.114 in an application: By a micro entity $318.00; By a small entity $636.00; By other than a small or micro entity $1,590.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE (continued examination) fees differ for first vs subsequent RCEs; see tables for subsequent-request amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for second or subsequent requests for continued examination (§ 1.17(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For filing a second or subsequent request for continued examination pursuant to § 1.114 in an application: (table referenced — amounts provided in the rules' tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent RCEs incur higher fees; consult full fee table for exact amounts.
